verses.commentary: I saw the Lord standing by the altar. Fifth vision. God himself present at the sanctuary, commanding destruction. Strike the pillars so the building collapses on worshipers. No escape for any survivor.
Though they dig to Sheol, my hand takes them. Though they climb to heaven, I bring them down. Vertical escape impossible. The cosmos offers no hiding place from God.
Though they hide on Carmel's top, I hunt them. Though they hide at the sea bottom, the serpent bites them. Highest mountain, deepest sea. No corner of creation provides refuge.
Though driven into exile, the sword follows. I will keep my eye on them for harm, not good. Even captivity brings no safety. God's attention, usually a blessing, now a curse.
The Lord Almighty touches the earth and it melts. Another hymn of power. The land heaves like the Nile. At a touch, solid ground becomes liquid. This is the God who judges.
He builds his palace in the heavens, sets its foundation on earth. Cosmic architecture. He calls the sea and pours it on land. Floods at command. The Lord is his name.

Are you not like the Cushites to me? A shocking comparison. Distant Ethiopia, unknown to Israel. I brought Philistines from Caphtor, Arameans from Kir. God moved all nations. Israel's exodus is not unique. Election does not mean exclusive divine activity.

The eyes of the Lord are on the sinful kingdom. I will destroy it from the face of the earth. But, crucial turn, I will not totally destroy the house of Jacob. Destruction but not annihilation. Judgment but not extinction.
I will shake Israel among the nations like grain in a sieve. Scattered but sifted. Not a pebble reaches the ground. The valuable preserved, the worthless discarded. Exile as purification.
All the sinners among my people will die by the sword. Those who say disaster will not touch us. False security is fatal. Those who trust their immunity are most vulnerable.

In that day I will restore David's fallen tent. The turn to hope. The dynasty collapsed but will be rebuilt. Broken walls repaired, ruins restored. Acts 15:16 quotes this for Gentile inclusion in the church.

They will possess the remnant of Edom and all nations that bear my name. Expansion beyond Israel. Nations bearing God's name included. The restoration is larger than the original. James sees this fulfilled in Gentile believers.

The reaper will be overtaken by the plowman. Harvest so abundant it overlaps with planting. New wine dripping from mountains, flowing from hills. Hyperbolic fertility. What was cursed is overwhelmingly blessed.

I will bring my people back from exile. They will rebuild ruined cities and inhabit them. Vineyards planted and enjoyed. Gardens made and eaten from. Reversal of 5:11 where they built but never lived, planted but never drank.

I will plant Israel in their own land. Agricultural metaphor for permanent settlement. Never again uprooted from the land I gave them. The book that began with earthquake and uprooting ends with planting and permanence. Final word: says the Lord your God. Covenant language restored. Judgment gives way to relationship.
